conflicts.point: Whether semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure serves as the sole enforceable choke point for governing frontier artificial intelligence.

positions.stance: Physical semiconductor fabrication facilities remain the only verifiable and auditable control point for frontier models.
Hardware-focused controls miss decentralized algorithmic distribution and post-fabrication software optimization.

conflicts.point: Whether pre-market deployment halts and compute caps protect public safety or function as regulatory moats protecting industry incumbents.

positions.stance: Rigid deployment thresholds are necessary to prevent systemic risks and unaligned AI behavior from scaling unchecked.
Compute thresholds and compliance standards act primarily as regulatory barriers that shield dominant technology firms from competition.

verdicts.conflict: Whether semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure serves as the sole enforceable choke point for governing frontier artificial intelligence.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position relies on verifiable customs data and export logs for extreme ultraviolet lithography systems. The accelerationist counter-argument correctly identifies software routing workarounds, but lacks equivalent empirical proof that decentralized algorithms can scale without dense hardware clusters.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-market deployment halts and compute caps protect public safety or function as regulatory moats protecting industry incumbents.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position accounts for historical industrial regulation precedents where compliance mandates systematically shielded large firms from antitrust enforcement. The safetyist stance narrowly focuses on tail-risk mitigation without addressing the structural market consolidation caused by high compliance costs.
